Lat/Long: 34.895216, -76.854798 (Approximated from establishment)
Reported Sheen Size: 3 feet by 75 feet (area 225 sq. ft.)
SkyTruth Minimum Estimate: 0.01 gallons
Report DescriptionCALLER STATES AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF DIESEL WAS RELEASED INTO THE NUESE RIVER FROM A BARGE. LAST FRIDAY, A CONTRACTOR WITH A 2 PART PUMP DREDGE BARGE WAS DOING SOME WORK, AND ISSUES ARISED WITH THE BARGE. THE BARGE WAS LEFT ALONG THE SHORE ON FRIDAY AS A PRECAUTION WITH ABSORBENT BOOM ALONGSIDE. AT THAT TIME THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF A RELEASE AND THE BARGE WAS SITTING ON THE BOTTOM. AT 1000, TODAY, A SHEEN FROM DIESEL WAS SEEN COMING FROM THE BARGE DUE TO INCLEMENT WEATHER CONDITIONS. THE BARGE HAS TWO 300 GALLON CAPACITY TANKS BUT THEY ARE ESTIMATING THAT THERE WAS APPROX. 150 GALLONS OF DIESEL ONBOARD. IT IS SUSPECTED THAT THE RELEASE MAY HAVE BEEN COMING FROM A U-SHAPED VENT PIPE DURING THAT INCLEMENT WEATHER.

ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATED THAT A TANKER TRUCK SLID ON ICE AND TURNED OVER. BECAUSE OF THIS (1500) GALLONS OF GASOLINE RELEASED ONTO SOIL AND A STORM DRAIN AT THE LOCATION. THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR ROAD CLOSURES IN CONNECTION TO THIS INCIDENT.
